data.cultural_impact: The name Mattie, originally derived from the Hebrew name Mattiyah, has been used to convey the idea of a divine gift, and has been a part of many cultures throughout history. It has been widely used in the English-speaking world, and is most famously associated with Saint Matthew the Evangelist, one of the twelve apostles of Jesus. This name holds a significant place in Christian tradition and history.
data.spiritual_significance: Similarly to its original Hebrew meaning ‘gift of God,’ the name Mattie carries a deep spiritual significance. This name is a reminder of the gift of faith that God bestows upon us, the gift of the presence of the Holy Spirit, and the ultimate gift of salvation. It serves as a reminder that we are all blessed by God, and that we should strive to live our lives in a way that reflects His love and mercy. As Christians, we are all called to be a gift to the world, using our talents and abilities to serve and uplift others in the name of Christ. By embracing our identity as a child of God, we are able to find purpose, meaning, and joy in our lives.

historical_references.reference: The name Mattie has been used throughout Christian history by saints, scholars, and faithful believers who exemplified its meaning.

modern_usage.modern_context: Mattie is a common name for girls in the United States, especially in the southern states. It is a variant of the name Matilda, which means 'mighty in battle'. In modern usage, Mattie is often used as a nickname or a short form of Matilda. It is also a popular name on social media platforms.
